questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How ice may have helped life begin
Why ice melts so quickly in hot weather
The first dinosaurs that lived on Earth
How to build and launch a space telescope
questions.why: They discuss a discovery that scientists think could explain the origins of life on Earth, and how ice fits in.

questions.q: What did the James Webb Space Telescope recently detect?
options: A new planet covered in liquid water
The coldest ices ever found in space
Signs of life on one of Jupiter's moons
A large comet about to hit the Earth
questions.why: Neil says it detected the coldest ices ever in outer space.

options: Full of tiny plants and small animals
Hot and dry, with no water at all
Covered in thick ice and frozen gases
Watery, with gases but no oxygen
questions.why: Sam describes a watery environment of oxygen-free gases and chemicals.

questions.q: According to Professor Melissa McClure, how did basic molecules like water and CO2 reach Earth?
options: In rain from the atmosphere
From volcanoes
In ice carried by comets
From the Sun's light
questions.why: She says those molecules were definitely brought to Earth by ices in comets.

questions.q: What might have turned these molecules into more complex ones, according to Professor McClure?
options: Heat from the ground or lightning
Very freezing temperatures in space
Strong wind and heavy rain for years
Plants growing on them over time
questions.why: She says they may have reacted with geothermal heat or a lightning strike.

questions.q: What makes a molecule a 'complex organic molecule', according to Professor McClure?
options: It contains water
It is found in organic food
It is very cold
It contains a carbon atom
questions.why: She says if they have a carbon atom in them, they're complex organic molecules.

questions.q: Why does Professor McClure mention alcohols like ethanol?
options: To warn listeners about drinking alcohol
To give simple examples of such molecules
To explain how comets are made from ice
To show that alcohol exists on Jupiter
questions.why: She says simple alcohols like methanol or ethanol, 'like what you would drink', are complex organic molecules.

questions.q: According to the theory, what created the first living cells?
options: A single huge lightning strike on the sea
Dinosaurs eating plants and spreading seeds
Reactions when molecules met the soup
Ice melting slowly in the warm oceans
questions.why: Sam says organic molecules meeting the primordial soup produced a chain reaction that created the first cells.
